title: Animate a pixel sprite
description: Animate an EXISTING pixel-art sprite (yours or one made here) from a description of the motion. Each frame is a pixel-art edit of the enlarged sprite, snapped back onto the sprite's own pixel grid and its own palette, so the frames match the original exactly in resolution and colours. Frames + sheet + atlas + GIF.
prompt_guide: Call the animate_pixel tool with the sprite's PNG and the motion: 'swinging the sword down in front of him', 'bouncing up and down, squashing when it lands', 'the flame flickering'. For the best result give `poses`: one short description per frame of what changes (the agent can write these from the user's description). Walk / run / idle / attack / jump / hurt / death / cast in the description use the built-in key poses.

param_help.model: diffusion model file (the preset normally picks it)
param_help.steps: sampling steps (the distilled models are made for 4 / 8)
param_help.candidates: takes generated in one batch; the best match to the prompt that passes the checks is kept
param_help.frame_candidates: takes per frame; the one most like the character reference is kept
param_help.frames: number of frames (0 = the motion's own count; 4 for a described motion)
param_help.poses: your own pose description per frame (a list); overrides the action's built-in poses
param_help.fps: playback speed written into the atlas
param_help.room: animate_pixel: free space around the sprite for swings and jumps, as a share of the canvas
param_help.canvas_size: animate_pixel: working canvas in pixels the sprite is enlarged onto
param_help.include_original: animate_pixel: put the untouched sprite in as frame 0
param_help.pad: animate_pixel: empty pixels kept around the animation's bounding box
param_help.procedural: animate_pixel: auto = bounce/squash, bob/float, breathe, shake, pulse and flash are done exactly in code (no AI); off = always redraw with the model; or name one of those motions
param_help.motion_amount: animate_pixel: how strong a procedural motion is (0.5 - 2)
param_help.keep_outline: animate_pixel: auto = if the sprite has a 1-pixel dark outline, every redrawn frame gets it back
param_help.remove_background: cut the subject out with BiRefNet (transparent PNG)
param_help.defringe: re-colour soft edges so no grey halo shows on dark backgrounds
param_help.rank_by_clip: rank the takes by how well they match the prompt (CLIP)
param_help.keep_candidates: keep every take in .spriteforge/<name>/ next to the result
param_help.normal_map: also write <name>_normal.png (2D lighting: Godot CanvasTexture, Unity 2D lights) and a lit preview
param_help.normal_strength: how pronounced the relief of the normal map is (0.5 subtle - 2 strong)
param_help.normal_y: up = OpenGL convention, green points up (Godot, Unity); down = DirectX
